MAJOR: `# noqa: E402` was moved (not duplicated) off `from core import backlog` in design_pack.py, functional_spec.py, and spec_pack.py; both imports sit after the sys.path loop, so the backlog import is now an unmarked E402. Design contract states "rejected status returns not-enforced"; no test covers this precedence.

The live/unknown assertions call `mod._cfg()` and depend on repo config (`enforce_from: 2026-11-07`, `enforce_items`), so a config date bump or adding `BI-TEST-0001` silently flips `test_live_statuses_still_enforced`/`test_unknown_status_still_enforced`. AC-4 proof is a source-string grep (`"gate_status.should_skip" in Path(mod.__file__).read_text()`); it passes if the token appears in a comment/docstring and does not demonstrate runtime invocation. A monkeypatch/identity assertion on the imported callable would be behavioral.
Diff modifies `scripts/dev/gen_docs_index.py`, which is not in the approved `affected_files` / `review_scope.files` list — an undeclared change relative to the approved contract.
NIT: `should_skip` strips and lowercases while the sibling `("new", "draft", "triaged")` check is case-sensitive, so `"Rejected"` skips but `"New"` does not; the normalization asymmetry is undocumented.
No log/metric distinguishes a terminal-skipped item from an absent one; design C-4 promises only "checked count", so a silently skipped item is not diagnosable from gate output.
Design doc `### Tests` section lists only 3 of the 5 test functions; `test_gates_share_the_terminal_predicate` and `test_terminal_status_set_is_explicit` are referenced only in the controls table.
SUMMARY: Implementation satisfies AC-1 through AC-4 at face value: one shared `gate_status.should_skip` predicate, four explicit terminal statuses, and tests spanning all three gates for terminal/live/unknown plus predicate reuse.

Top risks are the E402 noqa regression across three gate files (may break the very precheck baseline this item exists to restore) and the `enforce_items` override that can still force terminal items through enforcement.
Secondary gaps: config-coupled tests, source-string-based AC-4 proof, and an undeclared `gen_docs_index.py` edit; no blocker-level security, data, or language-rule violation.
